sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: System design interview questions are the differentiator for senior and staff Java backend roles — capacity estimation, the building blocks (load balancers, caches, queues, databases, CDNs), data partitioning, replication and consistency, rate limiting, idempotency at scale, designing for high availability, and the trade-offs that show up in every system-design round (latency vs throughput, consistency vs availability). This page covers the fundamentals; for full case studies (URL shortener, Twitter feed, distributed cache) see the System Design Problems page.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Always answer in **5 steps** — never skip a step.

1. **Requirements** (functional + non-functional + scale).
2. **Capacity** (QPS, storage, bandwidth).
3. **API + data model**.
4. **High-level design** (boxes + arrows).
5. **Deep dive** on the bottleneck the interviewer cares about.

Cite **CAP** + **PACELC** when consistency is on the line.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Latency vs throughput** — they trade against each other; cite p99 not avg.
- **Sharding** is a reorg, not an optimisation — earn it.
- **Cache** before sharding; **read replicas** before sharding.
- **Idempotency at scale** — keys + TTL + DB unique constraint.
- **Back-of-envelope numbers** — 1 GB/s ≈ 8 Gbps; 1 ms = 1 disk seek; 100 µs = 1 SSD read.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"At <X QPS, Y GB / day> I'd start with a load balancer in front of stateless app servers, a primary DB with read replicas, Redis for hot reads, Kafka for async work. The bottleneck will be <DB | cache | network> — the deep dive lives there."*
